title: Rational numbers
competency: Describe rational numbers, tell kinds of fractions apart and write fractions in simplest form.

keywords.def: A number that can be written a/b with integers a, b and b ≠ 0. The set is written ℚ.
A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator, such as 3/4.
A fraction whose numerator is at least its denominator, such as 7/3.
A whole number with a proper fraction, such as 5¼.
a/b is in simplest form (lowest terms) when GCF(a, b) = 1.
Numbers whose GCF is 1, such as 8 and 15.

en.text: Dividing one integer by another does not always give an integer. So we use a bigger set. A rational number can be written a/b, where a and b are integers and b is not 0. Every integer is rational, because n = n/1.

am.text: አንድን ኢንቲጀር በሌላ ማካፈል ሁልጊዜ ኢንቲጀር አይሰጥም። ስለዚህ ትልቅ ስብስብ እንጠቀማለን። ምክንያታዊ ቁጥር a/b ተብሎ ሊጻፍ ይችላል፤ a እና b ኢንቲጀሮች ሲሆኑ b ዜሮ አይደለም። እያንዳንዱ ኢንቲጀር ምክንያታዊ ነው፤ ምክንያቱም n = n/1 ነው።

screens.title: Divide some integers
screens.text: Take the integers 7, −2, 6, 0 and −3. Try these four divisions: 6 ÷ (−3), 0 ÷ 7, 7 ÷ 6 and −2 ÷ 7.
screens.ask: How many of the four answers are integers? Take a guess.
screens.after:
6 ÷ (−3) = −2: an integer.
0 ÷ 7 = 0: an integer.
7 ÷ 6 = 7/6 and −2 ÷ 7 = −2/7: not integers.
So two of the four answers are integers. Read on.

screens.title: Activity 1.9: what happens?
paras: But 7 ÷ 6 = 7/6 and −2 ÷ 7 = −2/7. These are not integers.
Dividing integers does not always give an integer. So we need a bigger set: the rational numbers.

screens.title: Definition 1.5 · Rational numbers
paras: A number that can be written as a/b is a rational number. Here a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
The set of rational numbers is ℚ = {a/b : a, b ∈ ℤ and b ≠ 0}.
−6 = −6/1 and 0 = 0/1. So every integer is rational. So is every natural number: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ.
screens.note: Figure 1.2: natural numbers sit inside the integers, which sit inside the rational numbers.

screens.title: Figure 1.2: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ
screens.ask: Tap a circle. Then tap each number.
rings: Any a/b with a, b integers and b ≠ 0.
numbers: A fraction that is not an integer.
5 = 5/1, a natural number, so it is in all three sets.

screens.title: Name it
defs: A number a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0. The set is ℚ.

screens.title: Spot the odd one
screens.text: Rational numbers: which number is NOT rational?
screens.why:
A rational number is a/b with a, b integers and b ≠ 0.
−6 = −6/1, 0 = 0/1 and 13/4 all fit.
5/0 has denominator 0, which is not allowed.
So 5/0 is not a rational number (it is not a number at all).
screens.clue: Read the condition on b in Definition 1.5.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: Natural numbers and ℚ: every natural number is also a rational number.
screens.why:
Take any natural number, for example 4.
Write it with denominator 1: 4 = 4/1.
4 and 1 are integers and 1 ≠ 0.
So 4 is rational. This works for every n: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ. True.
screens.clue: Can you write 4 as a fraction with denominator 1?

screens.title: Write an integer as a/b
screens.why:
Dividing by 1 leaves a number unchanged.
So −6 ÷ 1 = −6.
That means −6 = −6/1.
Every integer n can be written as n/1.
screens.clue: Which number can you divide by and leave −6 unchanged?

screens.title: Sharing injera
screens.text: Abebe shares 3 injera equally among 4 friends.
screens.ask: Division as a fraction: each friend gets ___ of an injera.
screens.why:
Sharing means dividing: 3 ÷ 4.
As a fraction, 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4.
Check: 4 friends × 3/4 = 12/4 = 3 injera.
So each friend gets 3/4. It is rational, but not an integer.
screens.clue: Write the division 3 ÷ 4 as a fraction.
screens.worked: Each friend gets 3 ÷ 4 of an injera. As a fraction this is 3/4.

ideas.name: Kinds of fractions and simplest form

en.text: In a proper fraction the top is smaller than the bottom, like 7/8. In an improper fraction the top is at least the bottom, like 7/3. A mixed fraction is a whole number with a proper fraction, like 5¼. A fraction is in simplest form when top and bottom have GCF 1.

am.text: በትክክለኛ ክፍልፋይ ላዩ ከታቹ ያንሳል፤ ለምሳሌ 7/8። ትክክለኛ ባልሆነ ክፍልፋይ ላዩ ቢያንስ ከታቹ እኩል ነው፤ ለምሳሌ 7/3። ድብልቅ ክፍልፋይ ሙሉ ቁጥርና ትክክለኛ ክፍልፋይ ነው፤ ለምሳሌ 5¼። የላይና የታች ትልቁ የጋራ አካፋይ 1 ሲሆን ክፍልፋዩ በቀላሉ ቅርጽ ነው።

screens.title: Sort these fractions
screens.text: Before you read, sort by feel. Is the top smaller, or not? Is there a whole number in front?
screens.after:
Top smaller: 7/8 and 2/9.
Top not smaller: 7/3 and 6/1.
Whole number with a fraction: 5¼.
Read on to learn the names of these kinds.

screens.title: Note: kinds of fractions
paras: Let x = a/b be a fraction with a and b positive.
(i) If a < b, x is a proper fraction.
(ii) If a ≥ b, x is an improper fraction.
(iii) A whole number with a proper fraction, such as 5¼, is a mixed fraction.
Example 2. 7/8 and 2/9 are proper. 7/3 and 6 (= 6/1) are improper. 5¼ is mixed.
screens.note: The book states (i) and (ii) for any integers a and b. They are meant for positive numbers: by the book's rule, −5/2 would count as proper because −5 < 2.

screens.title: Simplest form
paras: (iv) x = a/b is in simplest form (lowest terms) when GCF(a, b) = 1.
That is, a and b are relatively prime.

screens.title: 18/24 and 3/4 are the same size
screens.after: Both bars shade the same length. GCF(18, 24) = 6, and 18/24 = (18 ÷ 6)/(24 ÷ 6) = 3/4.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Numerator smaller than denominator, such as 7/8.
Numerator at least the denominator, such as 7/3 or 6/1.
A whole number with a proper fraction, such as 5¼.
a/b with GCF(a, b) = 1. Also called lowest terms.

screens.title: Which is improper?
screens.text: Kinds of fractions: which is an improper fraction?
screens.why:
Improper means the numerator is at least the denominator.
11/4: 11 > 4, so it is improper.
3/7 is proper: 3 < 7.
2⅓ is a mixed fraction, and 0.5 is a decimal.
screens.clue: Compare the top and bottom numbers.

screens.title: Mixed to improper
screens.text: Change a mixed fraction to an improper fraction: l m/n = l + m/n = (l × n + m)/n.
steps: Start with 3¼. Here l = 3, m = 1 and n = 4.
Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 3 × 4 = 12.

screens.title: Example 3 in bars: 3¼ = 13/4
screens.after: 3 wholes are 12 quarters. Add 1 more quarter: 13 quarters. So 3¼ = 13/4.

screens.title: Simplest form?
screens.text: Simplest form: is 18/24 in simplest form?
screens.why:
18/24 is in simplest form only if GCF(18, 24) = 1.
Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24.
GCF(18, 24) = 6, not 1.
Divide top and bottom by 6: 18/24 = 3/4.
So no: it simplifies to 3/4.

screens.title: Mixed to improper
screens.why:
Use (l × n + m)/n with l = 2, m = 1, n = 3.
Multiply: 2 × 3 = 6.
Add the numerator: 6 + 1 = 7.
So 2⅓ = 7/3.
screens.clue: Multiply the whole number by 3, then add the numerator.

screens.title: Coffee in the market
screens.text: Hirut buys 1¾ kg of coffee at Merkato.
screens.ask: Mixed to improper fraction: she buys ___ kg.
screens.why:
1¾ means l = 1, m = 3, n = 4.
1 × 4 = 4 quarters in the whole.
4 + 3 = 7 quarters.
So 1¾ kg = 7/4 kg.
screens.clue: Use (l × n + m)/n with l = 1, m = 3, n = 4.

screens.title: Lowest terms
screens.why:
Find GCF(35, 45): 35 = 5 × 7 and 45 = 5 × 9, so the GCF is 5.
Divide the top: 35 ÷ 5 = 7.
Divide the bottom: 45 ÷ 5 = 9.
GCF(7, 9) = 1, so 35/45 = 7/9 is in simplest form.
screens.clue: Divide top and bottom by GCF(35, 45).

items.text: (a) Integers and rational numbers: every integer is a rational number.
items.why:
Any integer n can be written as n/1.
n and 1 are integers, and 1 ≠ 0.
So n fits the definition a/b. Example: 5 = 5/1.
True.

items.text: (b) Simplest form: the simplest form of 35/45 is 9/7.
items.why:
GCF(35, 45) = 5.
35 ÷ 5 = 7 and 45 ÷ 5 = 9.
So 35/45 = 7/9.
9/7 has top and bottom swapped. False.

items.text: (c) Adding rational numbers: for a, b, c, d ∈ ℤ with b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0, a/b + c/d is a rational number.
items.why:
Use the common denominator bd: a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/(bd).
ad + bc is an integer, and bd is an integer.
b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0, so bd ≠ 0.
So the sum has the form p/q with q ≠ 0. True.
items.clue: Add the fractions using denominator bd.

items.text: (d) Mixed fractions: the simplest form of 5 2/4 is 11/2.
items.clue: Change to an improper fraction first, then simplify.

items.text: 3. Zebiba measures a table as 54 cm and 4 mm.
items.ask: Write the measurement as a fraction in lowest terms: ___ cm.

items.text: 4. A rope 5⅓ m long is cut into 4 equal pieces.
items.ask: Divide a mixed fraction: each piece is ___ m long.
items.why:
Change to improper: 5 × 3 + 1 = 16, so 5⅓ = 16/3.
Divide by 4: 16/3 ÷ 4 = 16/12.
Simplify by 4: 16/12 = 4/3.
So each piece is 4/3 m = 1⅓ m. Check: 4 × 4/3 = 16/3.
items.clue: Change 5⅓ to an improper fraction first.
items.worked: 5⅓ = 16/3. Then 16/3 ÷ 4 = 16/12 = 4/3. So each piece is 1⅓ m.

test.text: Sets of numbers: which set contains all the others: ℕ, ℤ or ℚ?
test.why:
Every natural number is an integer: ℕ ⊆ ℤ.
Every integer n = n/1 is rational: ℤ ⊆ ℚ.
So ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ.
ℚ contains the other two.

test.ask: Mixed to improper: 3¼ as an improper fraction is ___

test.text: Simplest form: 8/15 is in simplest form.
test.why:
8 = 2 × 2 × 2 and 15 = 3 × 5.
They share no prime, so GCF(8, 15) = 1.
8 and 15 are relatively prime.
So 8/15 is in simplest form. True.

notes.text: Kinds of fractions: the book states (i) and (ii) for any integers a and b. They are meant for positive numerators and denominators: by the book's rule, −5/2 would count as proper because −5 < 2.
Exercise 1.10 item (c) in the printed book does not say b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0. Without that, a/b and c/d might not be numbers. The lesson adds the condition.
Exercise 1.10 Q2 (show that a product of rationals is rational) is a proof and is not turned into an item.

screens.title: Find GCF(18, 24)
screens.text: The GCF is the largest number that divides both numbers.

screens.title: Your turn
screens.text: Greatest common factor: what is GCF(35, 45)?
screens.why:
35 = 5 × 7.
45 = 5 × 9 = 3 × 3 × 5.
The only shared prime is 5.
So GCF(35, 45) = 5.
